approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from previously accepted scored molecules. Score-band parent draws feed connected-fragment crossover and ordinary local mutations, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Its graph checker sanitizes and reparses each offspring. A second admission step verifies a stable canonical identity, normalizes confirmed graph-equivalent aliases and rejects unstable identities before duplicate checks build the surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to all earlier accepted scores uses folded counts of local molecular environments; correlated posterior draws allocate the announced evaluation batch. Real accepted feedback updates the prediction archive and the greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove the active stable-identity admission step while keeping its original checks as passive diagnostics. The original checked graph and its returned string will pass directly to the existing novelty, pool and emission bookkeeping. This isolates the retained identity component; the other current siblings change the count representation, donor construction or posterior allocation. An older identity control only normalized two unselected aliases, whereas the current Parent rejects one unstable representation. The new control follows any affected candidate through pool entry, selection and actual evaluator feedback. A natural identity failure remains evidence, and only complete exposed matched runs can answer the endpoint-contribution question.

observed_bottleneck: The retained stable-admission component has an unresolved current-Parent contribution, not a demonstrated score bottleneck or universal safety property. The actual n-62daf219c70a summaries and run logs contain all 15 successful current-profile sessions, 4,500 oracle evaluations including 4,350 accepted offspring, zero external invalid/duplicate attempts, macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. The read-only archived-log audit in .slots/r0017-03-ablation-L01/plan-evidence-audit.json counts each outer attempt once, excluding repeated emitted receipts: 75,961 attempts, 75,958 unchanged-stable identities, two inherited checker failures and one rejected_unstable_confirmation, with 69,600 pooled entries in 435 full pools and 6,358 local duplicates. The rejection is seed 0, drd2_docking, batch 29, attempt 60, run log line 5977; its next serialization differs from the checked raw spelling and its confirmation returns to that raw spelling. The raw spelling is novel in both recorded emitted/initial and temporary-pool sets immediately before this attempt, so bypassing only this gate would expose it to the pool on that recorded state. This is a late conditional opportunity; its hypothetical selection, accepted score and continuation are unknown. The historical complete n-213e85380e04 control, under its older binary-posterior composition, has 75,484 otherwise valid attempts: 75,482 unchanged identities and two normalized-stable aliases. The aliases occur in seed 1 deco_hop batch 27 at attempts 123 and 152, pool indices 120 and 149; neither is emitted. Its original matched analysis reports identical molecular/score trajectories and all 15 endpoint deltas zero, with mean 0.5443738005952443 and SD 0.013310111166991866. Our read-only reproduction of all three affected archived inputs matches every nontiming identity receipt and preserves the supplied graph binary; the current and historical helper implementations are identical. That audit checks the saved cases only. The historical analysis also records 59 unstable sibling representations rejected in read-only probes, including one historically emitted case and five with unchanged fingerprints; these are conditional failure-mode evidence rather than new Child evaluations or a guarantee of failure prevention. The pinned catalog keeps downstream behavior and component contribution undetermined for the historical identity addition, and marks the current contribution gap open because the Parent composition/profile differ. Stable logged initial identities, two unselected aliases and one current rejection cannot establish universal safety, dispensability or a complete current endpoint effect.
hypothesis: Remove active stable-canonical pool normalization and rejection after the inherited graph checker, routing its original checked molecular object and raw returned identity through existing novelty, pool, emission and pending interfaces while retaining the original stable-admission helper only as a passive comparator.

finding_summary.headline: Removing stable identity admission changes seven evaluations but leaves every endpoint unchanged
finding_summary.insights:
An unselected pool member can still change which other molecules receive evaluations. Here the pool substitution and index shift changed the correlated allocation, so equal endpoints do not mean identical search behavior. This supplies current downstream exposure that the older two unselected stable aliases lacked. The zero endpoint effect is nevertheless narrow: the sole opportunity occurred in the last batch, after the existing best score was already reached. The changed labels did not train another model or seed further breeding.

The experiment does not establish that an unstable key is safe to emit. That boundary was never naturally exercised, and the missing-provenance guard still raises in an explicitly synthetic control using real archived feedback. Nor does admission removal establish better chemistry: the altered final choices include both a high-scoring halogen-free amine and retained reactive substituents, while the broader ring-geometry and stereochemical limitations remain. Earlier identity exposure, actual selection of an unstable representation and other parser conventions remain open. The observed component result does not establish universal dispensability or effects of combining sibling changes.
finding_summary.results:
The removal had a real admission effect. Among 75,958 checked Child attempts, one candidate had an alternating identity string that the Parent rejected. The Child admitted its original checked graph and raw key into the final docking pool. The candidate itself was never selected, emitted or scored, and its two spellings were not shown to be graph-equivalent. Its admission substituted one pool member and shifted 104 shared positions. With the same recorded random-normal draws and unchanged marginal predictions for shared candidates, the final allocation evaluated seven different molecules. Four of those new alternatives remained in the final population; none improved the incumbent. Fourteen of fifteen complete task/seed trajectories were identical.

All fifteen task runs completed with valid unique batches, successful feedback joins and no external rejection or identity exception. Every paired final score and every best-so-far sequence stayed unchanged. Mean endpoint score was 0.595670 in both nodes, with seed population SD 0.026593; all three paired seed changes were exactly zero, within the registered 0.002 allowance. The active bypass was confirmed and the complete exposed comparison supports a conditional no-material-effect endpoint contribution for the admission component.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines persist; one altered final batch leaves reactive bonds and doubtful ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: The Child n-59c7b21b8199 and matched Parent n-62daf219c70a both have complete Search Seed 0, 1 and 2 panels under the supplied profile: child_complete=true, paired_complete=true, with no profile mismatches. All thirty supplied Child and published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Each task has 900 records per node, including 870 optimizer proposals, and no task lacks trajectories. Fourteen of fifteen matched task/seed trajectories are identical in every parsed record field. The exception is drd2_docking seed 0: eight row positions differ starting at evaluation 292, with seven Child-only and seven Parent-only evaluated identities in the final batch. All common identities retain their recorded scores, all fifteen best_so_far sequences are identical, and the final best molecules are shared. Equal endpoints therefore coexist with a small evaluated-chemistry difference; they do not establish complete trajectory identity. The output consists of substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Median optimizer heavy-atom counts, in the fixed task order, are 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27 in both nodes. Child ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9644 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9552 to 0.9736; these are text-feature incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Rings and aromaticity are rich. Structural diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, with narrower leading families within each seed. Recognizable amines, amides and heterocycles coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, peroxides, strained unsaturation and difficult bridges, leaving synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak overall. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence is zero throughout, despite available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. The absence of charge markers does not mean basic centres are absent. Heavy-atom counts and ring descriptions are read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 readings of the trusted trajectory structures, recorded in .slots/r0017-03-ablation-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json; neither graph perception nor score establishes synthesis, stability, geometry or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's retained optimum; the full panel was inspected. Supplemental log joins are kept separate from evaluated-molecule evidence in .slots/r0017-03-ablation-L01/molecular/identity_exposure_audit.json. At drd2_docking seed 0, batch 29, attempt 60, a crowded brominated methoxy polycyclic diamine has alternating serialization on the passive identity check. It enters the Child temporary pool at index 55; the corresponding Parent receipt rejects unstable confirmation. The raw and alternate spellings are absent from emission, accepted feedback, observed offspring, trusted trajectories and the reconstructed final population. It is unselected and has no recorded score; it is not included in cited_smiles. The passive receipt does not complete graph-equivalence checks, so this establishes an unstable representation in a pool, not equivalent graphs, an evaluated invalid molecule, a normalization benefit or endpoint contribution. The changed final pool contains one identity substitution; seven other Child molecules are evaluated, four remain in the final population, and none changes the incumbent. Retention is reconstructed from recorded feedback and the documented score/serial ordering, with all batch retention receipts checked; no new labels or counterfactual scores are produced. These exposure limits do not establish universal identity stability, safety or synthetic plausibility for either node. The transferable chemistry gaps retain their historical source and current observation conditions; chemistry association is not component attribution.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule has 25 heavy atoms: an ethyl/dimethyl/chloro-substituted indole linked through an N-hydroxy amide to a pyridyl ring, with fluorine attached to the indole nitrogen. Nearby leaders keep the fused aromatic/amide/azaaryl organization while changing N-S, N-halogen or halomethyl substituents. Seed 2 develops an indole-aryl vicinal-diketone family with aminomethyl substitution; seed 0 also reaches an amino-substituted cumulene attached to a fused aromatic system. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8805. These are mostly compact aromatic frameworks rather than ring-deficient fragments, but their local nitrogen and halogen environments make apparently familiar skeletons questionable synthetic targets. The same families and exact scores occur in the published Parent. All three current trajectories for this task are identical to the matched Parent in every parsed record field.
liabilities: Leading N-F, N-Cl and N-Br attachments to indole nitrogen are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogens; N-S substitution and halomethyl ethers also raise local reactivity concerns.
The N-hydroxy amide is a recognizable functional group but does not resolve the separate N-halogen liability on its scaffold.
The vicinal-dicarbonyl family has potentially reactive carbonyl chemistry, while the seed-0 leader contains a cumulated-double-bond segment; the scores do not demonstrate their stability.
missing_features: The leading examples do not establish conventional stable nitrogen substitution that preserves the favorable aromatic/carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement at the same score; an ordinary N-H indole amide is already present initially, so the generator is not incapable of that chemistry.
Chemically independent compact frameworks expressing the favorable functional-group arrangement are scarce among the leading examples; most vary substitutions on retained aromatic families.
The observed score ordering does not identify an exact missing pharmacophore, and does not establish that adding more donors, rings or halogens would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the N-hydroxy pyridyl-amide leader reaches 0.47411701813450596. Retaining only an N-fluoro amide on the trimethoxyindole, without its pendant aryl group, gives 0.0038788336708218928; ClCl reaches 0.0. The visible positive association therefore concerns the combined compact aromatic and carbonyl organization, not halogen presence alone. Two N-halogen/halomethyl variants share 0.4478476056206344 despite different peripheral placements. The seed-2 diketone leader scores 0.438972502037081, whereas a more substituted late relative scores 0.2537139094300773; extra polar substitution is not uniformly rewarded. The seed-0 cumulene leader scores 0.39405142067435733. These comparisons do not isolate a required reactive bond or an absent target-specific motif.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 30 heavy atoms and links a quinazoline-like fused aromatic region to a dense nitrogen-rich fused/bridged carbonyl-thione core. It bears aryl chlorine, an O-F group, and a fluorinated chloromethyl-ether side chain. An analogue replaces that side chain with difluoromethyl. Seed 1 favors linked aza-aromatic and oxygen-containing carbonyl rings with a carbon-linked nitrile and an O-linked cyanate. Seed 2 instead reaches aryl/heteroaryl assemblies bearing peroxide, nitrite and N=S functionalities. Mean proposal SMILES length is 59.1, with a maximum of 191, so compact leaders coexist with much larger proposals. The recognizable fused heterocycles do not make their reactive attachments or dense ring junctions synthetically routine. These are the same output families as the Parent, with no observed change in size or chemistry. All three current trajectories for this task are identical to the matched Parent in every parsed record field.
liabilities: The leader contains an aryl O-F bond, not an aryl C-F bond, and a chloromethyl ether; these require a different reactivity assessment from ordinary aromatic halogen substitution.
Thione functionality and crowded nitrogen-ring connectivity coexist with unspecified stereochemical possibilities; a graph and score do not establish a synthetic route.

Other high-scoring seed families retain O-linked cyanates, peroxide links, nitrite and N=S groups. These are specific local chemistry concerns, not proof that all heterocycles or nitriles are undesirable.
missing_features: Stable peripheral alternatives that preserve the favorable linked heterocyclic arrangement are not established among the best examples; local substituent ties leave room for alternatives without identifying one as better.
The dense fused/bridged core lacks demonstrated accessible geometry and stereochemical identity; higher ring count alone does not recover the favorable arrangement.

The compact leading family appears in one seed while other seeds retain different reactive families; the observed record does not demonstrate reliable coverage of that favorable chemical organization across seeds.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, a smaller nitrogen-carbonyl ring fragment scores 0.5093370681605975, and ethene sits at 0.5. The linked nitrogen-rich leader and its difluoromethyl analogue both reach 0.8561477222467935. A nearby connectivity variant reaches 0.8467276542724114, while the more extensively cross-linked final seed-0 structure falls to 0.564499484004128. This favors a particular combined heterocyclic arrangement in this sample, rather than simply adding rings, atoms or fluorine. Other seed leaders reach 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013 in different families. The tied peripheral variants do not show that an O-F bond is required, and the floor score should not be interpreted as evidence of useful chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The shared seed-0 leader is a 30-heavy-atom flexible tertiary amine connecting aromatic regions through alkyl chains, with phenol, methoxy, ethyl and propyl groups, a benzylic chloride and aromatic bromines. Seed 2 retains pyrrolidine-substituted dihydrobenzothiophene/biaryl frameworks with phenol or thiol and carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 1 retains an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine attached to a fluorinated cyclic aryl-ether region with another aminomethyl group. Median optimizer size is 31 heavy atoms; mean proposal SMILES length is 53.9, versus 53.8 in the Parent, and halogen-string incidence is 0.9851. Accessible aliphatic amines and aromatic surface are already present. Seed 1 and 2 trajectories are identical to the Parent. Seed 0 shares its leader but evaluates seven different identities in the last batch. These remain mostly large aryl cyclic amines: the four Child-only structures retained at the end are a smaller halogen-free aryl cyclic tertiary amine, an N-chloro arylamino/imine-containing polycycle, and two thiol-bearing aryl cyclic amines. A more extensively bridged diamine and an N-O-propyl hydroxylamine-like relative are evaluated but not retained. These evaluated molecules are distinct from the unselected identity-unstable pool candidate described above. Conventional amine and thioether scaffolds provide recognizable synthetic handles, but heavy halogen substitution, difficult ring connectivity, local reactive groups and unassigned stereochemistry remain.
liabilities: The shared flexible leader combines a potentially reactive benzylic chloride with substantial bromine/chlorine mass and hydrophobic alkyl segments; solubility, stability and selectivity are not characterized.

Some high-scoring relatives retain large ring closures or cyclic cumulated double bonds. The new final population also retains an N-chloro arylamino linkage and thiol-bearing macrocyclic arrangements, so changed exposure does not remove the local-chemistry and geometry concerns.

The pyrrolidine and fused thioether skeletons are recognizable, but unspecified stereochemistry prevents a fully defined molecular identity. High scores of halogen-free and conventional cyclic-amine examples are counterexamples to a universal need for the liabilities.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified forms of the successful saturated-ring and benzylic arrangements are absent, despite potentially stereogenic centres.

Consistent access to stable local substitutions and credible ring geometry while retaining the favorable amine/aromatic arrangement is not demonstrated. Other high-scoring cyclic-amine families and the retained halogen-free relative show that heavy halogenation and benzylic chloride are not universal requirements.
Protonation states are not explicitly resolved in the neutral SMILES, but basic centres are visibly present; the chemistry does not support simply adding an amine.

The sole passive identity anomaly provides pool-only evidence. It cannot establish what additional evaluated chemistry a stable or unstable spelling would supply, or whether either spelling denotes a synthetically plausible molecule.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197; the shared flexible tertiary-amine leader reaches 0.9999989177995104, the fused-thioether/pyrrolidine leader 0.9999934235240012, and the aminoalkyl cyclic-amine leader 0.9969753164881906. This associates reward with available aliphatic amines presented alongside aromatic regions, rather than nitrogen or halogen count alone. A smaller final fused-thioether amine scores 0.9947190867301007. In the changed final seed-0 batch, the smaller halogen-free aryl cyclic amine scores 0.985113028632634 and is retained; maximal halogen load and all aromatic appendages are not required for a high value. The new retained N-chloro structure scores 0.995037455456608, and the retained aryl-thiol and aliphatic-thiol relatives score 0.996556464675942 and 0.987328210885681. The N-O-propyl relative scores 0.509819259768488 and is not retained, but it differs at multiple positions and does not isolate an N-O penalty. The final-batch changes do not exceed the existing incumbent. High scores also coexist with a shared cyclic-cumulene relative. These are supplied objective values, not measurements of affinity, selectivity, stability or accessible conformation.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 29 heavy atoms and joins a propyl-substituted quinoline to a partially unsaturated, bridged nitrogen/oxygen ring system with N-methyl groups and carbonyls. Seed 1 uses related quinoline-linked amino/ether rings and dicarbonyl nitrogen rings; seed 0 reaches a densely bridged diaryl lactam containing an N-O bridge. Thus aromatic surfaces, saturated nitrogen centres and carbonyl acceptors are all represented. Mean proposal SMILES length is 52.6 and halogen-string incidence is 0.1241, much lower than in the other supplied families. Recognizable functional groups coexist with medium-ring bridges and difficult connectivity, so atom-count compactness alone does not establish an accessible synthesis. The same structures and gradients are already present in the Parent. All three current trajectories for this task are identical to the matched Parent in every parsed record field.
liabilities: Medium-ring closures, bridges and ring-bound unsaturation create synthesis and geometry questions despite moderate heavy-atom counts.

The diaryl leader contains an N-O bridge, and nearby variants introduce further N-O or N-N functionality; these require environment-specific assessment rather than treating all nitrogen substitutions as equivalent.
Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, so potential stereogenic saturated centres in these connected ring systems remain unspecified.
missing_features: The leading families do not demonstrate simpler, accessible connectivities that preserve the favorable arrangement of aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl regions at the same score.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of the saturated bridges and medium rings is unresolved.
Chemically independent alternatives are limited among leaders within each seed, although the different seed families prevent a claim of total scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329 and the leading quinoline/bridged-dicarbonyl structure reaches 0.22600312875247064. Extending its oxygen-containing ring segment gives 0.2243673789386108; a corresponding carbon-containing segment gives 0.22237557923837944. A different diaryl bridged lactam reaches 0.2258403994203931. These nearby values associate reward with the combined aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl organization more than with a unique local atom. Methane scores 0.0. The final seed-2 bridged relative scores 0.20735848908965118, while its retained incumbent remains higher. The record supplies no exact missing target motif and no evidence that increasing general ring or heteroatom richness will solve the remaining gap.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 26 heavy atoms. It contains an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring bearing imino and carbonyl groups, N-fluoroalkyl substituents, and a fluorinated five-membered carbocycle with an enolic hydroxyl and a cumulated sequence of double bonds. This leader has carbon-bound fluorine rather than an N-F bond, but its cyclic cumulene raises a substantial geometric concern. Seed 0 instead retains N-fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl heterocycles attached to anisole and a small unsaturated nitrogen ring. Seed 1 retains a related fused dione with phenol and fluorinated alkenyl substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.6; the cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0517. Compact size and abundant nitrogen do not resolve the difficult ring geometry or reactive substitutions. All of this chemistry is reproduced from the Parent. All three current trajectories for this task are identical to the matched Parent in every parsed record field.
liabilities: The cumulated sequence forced into a five-membered ring raises severe strain and synthetic-accessibility concerns.

Other leaders retain N-F bonds and small unsaturated nitrogen rings. The top molecule's lack of N-F is a real counterexample to a universal N-F requirement, not evidence that local reactivity is controlled throughout the output.
A sharp local score change can occur while the doubtful core remains unchanged; score sensitivity therefore cannot certify that core's chemical feasibility.
missing_features: Geometrically credible alternatives preserving the compact fluorinated/polar organization are not established at the leading score; the high-scoring noncumulated relative is an important counterexample to any claim that reward requires the cyclic cumulene.

The large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring and enolic representation lack demonstrated conformational and tautomeric identity; lowercase aromatic notation is not evidence of a stable aromatic conformation.
Explicit stereochemical identity of substituted saturated centres is absent, and the scores do not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore or justify importing one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The cyclic-cumulene leader reaches 0.7208853668418119, while a related noncumulated carbocycle with changed nitrogen substitution reaches 0.6725143757617169. This is not an isolated cumulene comparison and does not show that the cumulene is required. The strongest close contrast changes the leader's N-fluoromethyl substituent to N-hydroxymethyl with the rest of the cited framework unchanged: the score falls to 0.006653135242129762. The observed sensitivity is to that local substitution within that scaffold, not a universal requirement for fluorine. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.6510211907030741 and 0.4870057305679067 in other families. Isolated F and FF score 1.1043196211273875e-26 and 4.97400031457045e-24, respectively, so fluorination without molecular context is insufficient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in n-59c7b21b8199 against that matched Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task under the current frozen profile. Shared leaders contain N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F, halomethyl ethers or benzylic chloride; other seed leaders contain peroxide and cyanate groups. A newly evaluated N-chloro arylamino structure is retained in the changed final population. Conventional carbon-bound halogens and recognizable tertiary or cyclic amines also have high supplied scores, and a newly retained aryl cyclic amine is halogen-free. One fluorinated leader contains no N-F bond. These counterexamples make the concern environment-specific.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments when modifying useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware transformations and plausible local alternatives that retain favorable scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from feedback. Preserve ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful nitrogen centres where supported. Neither these structural associations nor the isolated pool-only spelling anomaly establish a universal filter benefit or identify which component caused a chemical liability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in n-59c7b21b8199 against that matched Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task under the current frozen profile. The shared fluorinated imino/carbonyl leader combines a small cyclic cumulene with a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring. Other leaders contain medium-ring bridges, and a shared aryl-amine relative contains cyclic cumulated double bonds. A noncumulated fluorinated relative, recognizable saturated cyclic amines, and a newly retained smaller aryl cyclic amine also receive high supplied scores. Difficult unsaturation and bridges therefore are not universal requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a representable ring graph from a geometrically credible unsaturation pattern or bridged topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring transformations sensitive to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, with alternative topologies that preserve learned favorable functional arrangements. Ring counts, aromatic notation and stable serialization cannot supply the missing geometric information. This supports assessing geometry, not blanket exclusion of small rings, fused systems or all ring formation; no causal score benefit is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in n-59c7b21b8199 against that matched Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task under the current frozen profile. Every task retains stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, while aryl/cyclic amines, fluorinated ring centres and bridged frameworks contain potentially stereogenic environments. The changed final-batch molecules do not resolve this gap. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but protonatable aliphatic amines are already present; charge representation is a separate issue.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry where a generated structure requires it, with appropriate treatment of achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Assess protonation and tautomerism separately. These records show unspecified molecular identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty, proof of instability, or a component-specific failure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in n-59c7b21b8199 against that matched Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task under the current frozen profile. Tiny halogen and hydrocarbon proposals reach observed floors, including late proposals, while useful scores occur for combinations of aromatic, carbonyl and amine regions. A more cross-linked final fused heterocycle scores below its compact leader. Conversely, a smaller fused-thioether amine remains high-scoring and a newly retained halogen-free aryl cyclic amine is smaller than the leading flexible aryl amine. Useful simplification is possible and smaller size is not intrinsically unfavorable.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain enough functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to guide transformations that preserve useful chemical context while simplifying or replacing dispensable portions. The missing capability is consistent control of context loss and elaboration, not the ability to generate small molecules. Neither a fixed minimum size nor a preference for larger structures follows from these conditional observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in n-59c7b21b8199 against that matched Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task under the current frozen profile. Leading examples repeatedly vary halogen placement, short side chains, carbonyl-adjacent groups or ring segments on retained aromatic-amide, fused-heterocycle, aryl-amine and bridged-dicarbonyl frameworks. The changed final batch mostly supplies further aryl cyclic-amine variants, including a useful smaller example. Different seeds produce different families and ring-string incidence is high throughout; this is limited leading-family coverage, not global collapse or an inability to make rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently produce chemically independent plausible alternatives to the leading scaffold family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer chemically independent feasible connectivities while preserving favorable functional-group relationships learned locally, then let feedback assess them. Distinct strings alone do not establish useful scaffold coverage. The observations do not identify a component responsible for convergence, show that the unselected identity anomaly expanded evaluated coverage, or guarantee a benefit from additional diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
